years.overview_en: Explore number, algebra, measurement, geometry, and statistics through pictures, short explanations, practice, and real activities. Choose a small set at a time.
years.overview_zh: Year 3完整来源目标映射的学习资源：40节，五领域，图片先带学，再选用练习、独立检查及隔日复习；实际活动目标另记家长观察。
years.age_guidance_zh: 面向数学进度为Year 3、可能仅6岁的孩子：降低文字负荷而非降低数学内容；读题帮助与数学提示区分。题库不要求一次做完，先看三帧图，做带学理解检查，每次选4至6题。可按单领域进入新内容，不以在读年级或整年复习作硬门槛。

years.overview_en: Explore whole-number structure, exact calculation, fractions and tenths, measurement, shapes, and data. Picture lessons lead into varied practice and later checks; hands-on goals need real activity.
years.overview_zh: 依据2026新西兰Year 4逐项展开：位值与运算、分数与十分位、货币、等式与规律、测量、几何及统计。40课提供图解、练习、独立检查与后续复习；实际操作目标另配活动观察。
years.age_guidance_zh: 面向进度较快的8岁学习者保持Year 4数学深度，短英文与先图后文降低阅读负担。可分次做题，不设速度达标；请成人观察实作与口头解释。数学年级不等于阅读年龄。

years.overview_en: Build number relationships, measure and make shapes, investigate data, and explore chance.
years.overview_zh: Year 5 全领域学习资源：用位值和数量关系连接数与运算，同时学习代数、测量、几何、统计与概率。
years.age_guidance_zh: 为能力超前的8岁儿童保留Year5数学范围；英文使用短句，一次一图。允许指图、点选和口头解释，阅读/工具操作支持与数学独立证据分开。

years.overview_en: Explore numbers and relationships, measure and transform shapes, investigate data, and reason about chance. Use pictures first, then practice, independent checks and later review.
years.overview_zh: Year 6 六领域资源：38节图示教学配套练习、独立检查、隔日新题与需要实际操作的活动；逐项覆盖官方120项知识和实践目标。
years.age_guidance_zh: 教学年级与阅读年龄分开。适用于需要Year 6数学挑战的儿童，尤其本项目6岁与8岁学习者：由成人按需朗读，允许指图和操作，每次选一个小目标。复杂课可拆开，活动不计时。

years.overview_en: Explore Year 7 mathematics through pictures, short explanations, full practice sets and real investigations. Choose 10, 15 or 20 practice questions; checks and later reviews are fresh.
years.overview_zh: 依据2026年新西兰Year 7数学与统计课程，覆盖139条知识与实践目标。37课以图示、简短英文、完整练习和可观察的动手活动展开；题目成绩与实际调查、作图、测量表现分开看待。
years.age_guidance_zh: 数学层级按Year 7安排，语言为年龄较小但数学超前的孩子降低阅读负担。家长可朗读或用中文解释情境，保留原有数学难度。无需按实际年龄退回低年级；可复习先修课，也可自由进入下一年级。建议每次先看一张图，再口述理由，最后独立练习。

years.overview_en: Explore the full Year 8 mathematics and statistics scope. Use visual explanations, complete practice sets, short checks, and real investigations.
years.overview_zh: 覆盖2026年新西兰Year 8数学与统计官方年度目标：数、代数、测量、几何、统计与概率。数值练习与亲手探究并行，家长可查看精确目标映射。
years.age_guidance_zh: 数学范围按Year 8保留，不因孩子实际年龄6岁或8岁降低。英文用短句、图与逐步提示；成人可读题、代写或听孩子口述。按理解调整节奏，必要时回看前置课；完成后可自主进入下一学习阶段，不用年龄或单次分数锁定进度。

lessons.goal_en: Read, build, and write numbers from zero to one thousand.
teaching_notes_zh: 先分开数值与数字所在位置；包含0、空位零与1000的四位结构。 适合数学超前的6岁孩子：先看图、可朗读题干；每次可分成4至6题小组，24题是可选练习库，不要求一次完成。提示后的表现与首次独立检查分开。

introduction_en: 367 lies between the neighbouring hundreds 300 and 400.
367 is past halfway, so the nearest hundred is 400.
To the nearest ten, the same number rounds to 370.

lessons.goal_en: Compare unit fractions from the same-sized whole.
teaching_notes_zh: 分母越大每份越小只在同样大的整体和单位分数情境下直接成立。 适合数学超前的6岁孩子：先看图、可朗读题干；每次可分成4至6题小组，24题是可选练习库，不要求一次完成。提示后的表现与首次独立检查分开。
introduction_en: We compare shares from wholes that have the same size.
One third covers more length than one sixth of this whole.
A larger denominator makes each unit fraction smaller.

items.diagram_alt_en: A solid cuboid is 5 cubes across, 4 deep and 2 high. How many MORE unit squares are in its top view than its front view?

steps_en: Build a cuboid three cubes across, two deep and one high.
Draw its front, side and top outlines.
Move your viewpoint without changing the solid.
Describe the solid so someone else can rebuild it.
activity.observe_zh: 观察不同视点与二维图的对应，以及口头描述；题目数面只是支撑，不等于所有空间可视化完成。

lessons.goal_en: Perform and describe one-step transformations.
teaching_notes_zh: 这里数值/选择题只识别变换；真实执行单步变换由活动观察。明确镜线和旋转中心。
introduction_en: A translation moves every point the same distance and direction.
A reflection places matching points equally far from the mirror line.
A rotation keeps one centre fixed while the shape turns.

lessons.title_zh: 连续测量数据的采集与分组
lessons.goal_en: Record measurements consistently, then place each value in one clear group.
teaching_notes_zh: 先指定单位与取整精度再采集。组边界用含下界、不含上界，既不漏也不重复；连续数据不是“所有小数”的同义词。
introduction_en: Measure every object the same way. State the required rounding precision.

Keep both answers on one row for each person.
Count each fruit-and-game combination.
Draw clustered bars with a title, category labels, zero-based frequency scale and a colour key.
Describe one within-group and one between-group comparison.

lessons.title_en: Measure and estimate with a benchmark
lessons.goal_en: Choose and use tools and benchmarks for length, mass, capacity, temperature and duration.

Check the unit and the value of each scale interval.
A difference helps improve the next estimate; it is not evidence of failure.

activity.title_en: Plan a journey and compare calendars
materials_en: Locally sourced maramataka or a Chinese lunar calendar
steps_en: Plan a trip and record departure, arrival and duration in both time systems.
Time a short real activity and express its duration in minutes and seconds.
Compare a solar calendar with a lunar or lunisolar calendar: identify how months relate to seasons or Moon phases.
With an adult, discuss how different communities use their calendar to organise activities.
activity.observe_zh: 观察时刻与时长区分、正午转换、跨小时计算；历法比较只记录理解与提问，不用数值答题认证文化知识。

materials_en: Category responses from a small survey
steps_en: Count each response once in a frequency table.
Draw a categorical dot plot and a bar graph.
Include group, title, labels and a frequency scale.
Ask someone to read the most common category and total.
activity.observe_zh: 检查图中数量与原数据一致，并让孩子解释为何这种图适合类别数据。实际作图能力单独记录。

lessons.goal_en: Choose graphs that preserve the relationship.
teaching_notes_zh: 成对类别图要保留两个变量和图例，堆叠条的总高与单个部分的高度不同。时间序列有顺序，趋势不能保证下一时刻一定继续。
introduction_en: Travel method and class are two categorical variables. Clustered bars compare classes within each travel category.
Stacking preserves both class counts and each travel method’s total; the legend names the groups.
A time-series graph pairs each time with a measurement; join points in time order.

introduction_en: Three red counters among ten identical counters give P(red) = 3/10.

introduction_en: In one set of 30 coin tosses, 17 are heads and 13 tails. These are observations, not a rule.
Experimental P(heads) is 17/30. A fair-coin model gives theoretical P(heads) = 1/2.

Toss at least 30 times and record every H or T.
Calculate experimental probabilities for both outcomes.

lessons.title_zh: 一百次以上与大数规律
lessons.goal_en: Compare every outcome with a theoretical model.
teaching_notes_zh: 大数规律谈稳定重复条件下的长期相对频数，不保证每增加一次就更接近，也不保证100次必定比30次接近。若装置有偏，长期靠近其真实概率，而不是自动靠近均等值。
introduction_en: In this example, 54 heads and 46 tails occur in 100 fair-coin trials.
The experimental values 0.54 and 0.46 are each 0.04 from the fair model’s 0.5.
For a stable fair process, long-run relative frequencies approach 0.5; individual steps can move away.

activity.title_en: Track at least one hundred trials
steps_en: Use the same coin and method for at least 100 tosses; retain all outcomes.
At 30, 60 and 100 trials, record cumulative H and T counts.
Calculate both relative frequencies and compare each with 1/2.
Plot trial count against each relative frequency.
Describe the overall pattern and any steps that move farther away; do not change the data.
activity.observe_zh: 必须实做至少100次，并逐个比较所有结果的实验与理论概率。可分多次完成，但规则保持不变。若本次结果没有更接近，应如实讨论而不伪造“大数规律成功”。

lessons.goal_en: Explain an unusual point and its effect on summaries.
teaching_notes_zh: 离群值不一定错，先查单位和情境。中位数比均值更抗极端值，但并非任何增删数据都绝对不变；偏态按长尾方向命名，极差会受极端值强烈影响。
introduction_en: Most values lie together; one unusually distant point may be an outlier.
A high outlier pulls the mean and stretches the range. The median is less affected, not always unchanged.
The long right tail gives positive skew. Check unusual observations before keeping or correcting them.

cards.question_en: Read, build, and write numbers from zero to one thousand.
cards.idea_en: Read, build, and write numbers from zero to one thousand.
steps_en: Hundreds, tens, and ones each have their own place.
Combine the values of the digits to name the whole.
Ten hundreds become one thousand, written with four digits.
cards.remember_en: The 4 sits in the tens column, so it is worth 40.

connects_to.label_en: Year 4 · A digit needs a place

cards.question_en: Count large collections using tens and hundreds.
cards.idea_en: Count large collections using tens and hundreds.
steps_en: Large equal groups help us count without losing our place.
Two hundreds, three tens, and four ones make 234.
Ten groups of one hundred can become one thousand.
cards.remember_en: 10 × 100 = 1000. The amount stays the same when we rename it.

cards.question_en: Compare whole numbers using place value and symbols.
cards.idea_en: Compare whole numbers using place value and symbols.
steps_en: First compare hundreds; if they match, compare the tens.
On this number line, 313 comes before 330.
The open side faces the greater number in a comparison.
cards.remember_en: Both numbers have three hundreds. Three tens are greater than one ten.

connects_to.label_en: Round to a nearby ten or hundred

cards.title_en: Round to a nearby ten or hundred
cards.question_en: Use halfway points to round to tens and hundreds.
cards.idea_en: Use halfway points to round to tens and hundreds.
steps_en: 367 lies between the neighbouring hundreds 300 and 400.
367 is past halfway, so the nearest hundred is 400.
To the nearest ten, the same number rounds to 370.
cards.remember_en: The gap to 400 is smaller. The nearest hundred is 400.

cards.question_en: Round both quantities to make a useful estimate.
cards.idea_en: Round both quantities to make a useful estimate.
steps_en: Round both numbers before adding to estimate the total.
Three hundreds and one hundred make about four hundreds.
The exact total, 402, is close to our estimate.
cards.remember_en: Estimate first, then use it to check whether an exact answer makes sense.

connects_from.label_en: Round to a nearby ten or hundred

cards.question_en: Count forwards and backwards with equal jumps.
cards.idea_en: Count forwards and backwards with equal jumps.
steps_en: Counting in fours means adding four with each jump.
Going backwards reverses the jumps; subtract four each time.
Adding ten changes the tens while keeping the ones.
cards.remember_en: Equal backward jumps subtract four every time.

cards.question_en: Use pairs and counting sequences to explain number patterns.
cards.idea_en: Use pairs and counting sequences to explain number patterns.
steps_en: Even numbers make pairs; odd numbers leave one unpaired.
Counting by threes alternates between odd and even totals.
Twos and fives meet at multiples of ten.
cards.remember_en: Odd plus three changes the pairing: the total becomes even.

cards.question_en: Find missing parts of one hundred and scale known facts.
cards.idea_en: Find missing parts of one hundred and scale known facts.
steps_en: The missing part joins the known part to make 100.
From 34, add six to 40, then sixty more.
Three plus four also helps us combine hundreds.
cards.remember_en: The known part and missing part must fill the whole of one hundred.

cards.question_en: Add within one thousand by exchanging equal place-value units.
cards.idea_en: Add within one thousand by exchanging equal place-value units.
steps_en: Place ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds.
Seven ones plus four ones make one ten and one one.
The exchanged ten joins the tens; the total is 191.
cards.remember_en: Ten ones become one ten, with one one left over.

cards.question_en: Rename units to subtract while keeping the whole unchanged.
cards.idea_en: Rename units to subtract while keeping the whole unchanged.
steps_en: Subtract matching place values, starting with the ones column.
Exchange one ten so thirteen ones can lose six ones.
Another exchange lets us subtract tens; check by adding back.
cards.remember_en: Exchanging changes how the amount is grouped, but not its value.

cards.question_en: Choose operations that match each change in a story.
cards.idea_en: Choose operations that match each change in a story.
steps_en: A bus starts with 28 children before anyone moves.
Twelve get on, then nine get off the bus.
The final amount is 31 children, not both changes added.
cards.remember_en: Getting on increases the number; getting off decreases it.

cards.question_en: Connect equal groups, repeated addition, and multiplication.
cards.idea_en: Connect equal groups, repeated addition, and multiplication.
steps_en: Each row has four counters, and there are three rows.
Repeated addition counts every row once, giving twelve counters.
Three groups of four can be written as three times four.
cards.remember_en: Three counts the equal groups. Four counts the dots in each group.

cards.question_en: Find group sizes or group counts, then check with multiplication.
cards.idea_en: Find group sizes or group counts, then check with multiplication.
steps_en: Twelve counters can be shared into three equal groups.
Each of the three groups receives exactly four counters.
Three groups of four rebuild twelve; zero groups cannot.
cards.remember_en: The whole and the number of groups are known; the group size is missing.

connects_to.label_en: Find one part of a quantity

cards.question_en: Split a two-digit number, multiply each part, then combine.
cards.idea_en: Split a two-digit number, multiply each part, then combine.
steps_en: Twenty-three is two tens and three ones in each row.
Two twenties make forty, and two threes make six.
Forty and six join to make the product forty-six.
cards.remember_en: Two tens and three ones make twenty-three. Multiply both parts.

cards.question_en: Show fractions in regions, sets, lengths, and on a number line.
cards.idea_en: Show fractions in regions, sets, lengths, and on a number line.
steps_en: This whole ribbon is divided into four equal parts.
Three of the four equal parts make three quarters.
Three quarter-steps on a number line reach the same fraction.
cards.remember_en: The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.

connects_to.label_en: Find one part of a quantity

cards.question_en: Compare unit fractions from the same-sized whole.
cards.idea_en: Compare unit fractions from the same-sized whole.
steps_en: We compare shares from wholes that have the same size.
One third covers more length than one sixth of this whole.
A larger denominator makes each unit fraction smaller.
cards.remember_en: Three equal pieces are larger than six equal pieces of the same cake.

cards.question_en: Compare the number of equal-sized fraction parts.
cards.idea_en: Compare the number of equal-sized fraction parts.
steps_en: Both strips use sixths, so their small pieces match.
Five sixths contains more equal pieces than two sixths.
With the same denominator, compare how many parts are counted.
cards.remember_en: Both fractions count sixths of the same-sized whole.

cards.question_en: Split parts again without changing the fraction’s amount.
cards.idea_en: Split parts again without changing the fraction’s amount.
steps_en: One half covers one of two equal parts.
Splitting each half into three pieces makes sixths.
Three sixths equals one half; six sixths fills the whole.
cards.remember_en: The amount stays fixed although the number and size of the pieces change.

cards.question_en: Combine or remove equal-sized parts within one whole.
cards.idea_en: Combine or remove equal-sized parts within one whole.
steps_en: All pieces here are eighths of the same whole.
Two eighths and three eighths make five eighths together.
Removing three eighths leaves two eighths; eighths stay eighths.
cards.remember_en: We count more eighths; we do not change the size of each piece.

cards.title_en: Find one part of a quantity
cards.question_en: Divide the whole into equal groups to find one share.
cards.idea_en: Divide the whole into equal groups to find one share.
steps_en: The whole has 42 counters before we make any shares.
The denominator six tells us to make six equal groups.
One sixth is seven; six groups of eight would make 48.
cards.remember_en: Share all 42 into six equal groups. Each group has seven.

cards.question_en: Repeat one known share to rebuild every equal part.
cards.idea_en: Repeat one known share to rebuild every equal part.
steps_en: One quarter contains three counters; this is just one part.
A whole made of quarters needs four equal groups.
Four threes make twelve; one quarter of twelve is three.
cards.remember_en: Four equal quarters make the whole. Repeat the group of three four times.

connects_from.label_en: Find one part of a quantity

cards.question_en: Build money amounts using dollars, cents, coins, and notes.
cards.idea_en: Build money amounts using dollars, cents, coins, and notes.
steps_en: One dollar contains one hundred cents, however coins are grouped.
Two dollars and fifty cents names dollars and leftover cents.
One five-dollar note and three two-dollar coins make eleven dollars.
cards.remember_en: A dollar is made of one hundred cents.

cards.question_en: Add costs and subtract them from the money paid.
cards.idea_en: Add costs and subtract them from the money paid.
steps_en: A six-dollar book and a three-dollar pen cost nine dollars.
Paying with twenty dollars leaves change after the nine-dollar cost.
Cost and change together must equal the amount paid.
cards.remember_en: The money kept as cost and returned as change together equal the payment.

connects_to.label_en: Year 4 · Work out cost and change

cards.question_en: Check both sides and find missing values in equations.
cards.idea_en: Check both sides and find missing values in equations.
steps_en: Both sides of an equals sign must have matching values.
In seventeen plus something equals thirty, find the missing part.
Thirteen fills the gap because seventeen plus thirteen makes thirty.
cards.remember_en: We may calculate either side. Equality means their values match.

cards.question_en: Find, continue, and create patterns with a consistent change.
cards.idea_en: Find, continue, and create patterns with a consistent change.
steps_en: These towers grow by adding two blocks each time.
Adding two to every term keeps the same growing pattern.
A pattern can also decrease by the same amount each time.
cards.remember_en: Every neighbouring pair differs by two.

cards.question_en: Estimate, measure, and compare lengths using shared units.
cards.idea_en: Estimate, measure, and compare lengths using shared units.
steps_en: Different hand sizes give different counts for the same length.
Centimetres give a shared unit; place the object at zero.
Nine centimetres is two centimetres longer than seven centimetres.
cards.remember_en: The zero mark is the start of the measured intervals.

connects_to.label_en: Year 4 · Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Choose tools and whole-number units for mass and capacity.
cards.idea_en: Choose tools and whole-number units for mass and capacity.
steps_en: A balance compares mass; shared gram units give a number.
Read the top of the water against the jug’s markings.
Eight hundred millilitres is more than six hundred millilitres.
cards.remember_en: Millilitres measure an amount of liquid a container holds.

cards.question_en: Measure and add all the sides around a boundary.
cards.idea_en: Measure and add all the sides around a boundary.
steps_en: Perimeter means the whole distance around the shape’s boundary.
A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides.
The boundary measures eighteen centimetres, including all four sides.
cards.remember_en: Perimeter adds the side lengths around the boundary.

cards.question_en: Cover rectangles with equal squares and count the surface units.
cards.idea_en: Cover rectangles with equal squares and count the surface units.
steps_en: Equal squares must cover the rectangle without gaps or overlaps.
There are three rows with four equal squares in each.
If each square is one square centimetre, the area is twelve.
cards.remember_en: Equal square units make the count a fair measure of area.

cards.question_en: Describe rotations about a point in either direction.
cards.idea_en: Describe rotations about a point in either direction.
steps_en: The arrow turns around its centre, keeping that point still.
Two quarter turns make a half turn in the same direction.
Four quarter turns make one full turn back to the start.
cards.remember_en: Four quarter turns complete one rotation back to the starting direction.

cards.question_en: Connect analogue hands, digital time, minutes past, and minutes to.
cards.idea_en: Connect analogue hands, digital time, minutes past, and minutes to.
steps_en: The short hand shows hours; the long hand counts minutes.
Twenty minutes after three is written as three twenty.
At three forty-five, fifteen minutes remain until four o’clock.
cards.remember_en: The long hand travels through sixty minute positions in one hour.

cards.question_en: Find elapsed time and choose useful units for events.
cards.idea_en: Find elapsed time and choose useful units for events.
steps_en: Duration measures the time between an event’s start and end.
Fifteen minutes to nine twenty-five, then ten more, make twenty-five.
Four quarter-hours make sixty minutes, which is one hour.
cards.remember_en: Duration is the elapsed time from start to end.

cards.question_en: Compare calendar units and notice the extra days.
cards.idea_en: Compare calendar units and notice the extra days.
steps_en: Weeks contain seven days; fifty-two full weeks contain 364 days.
Months vary; ordinary years have 365 days, and leap years have 366.
Decades, centuries, and millennia group ten, hundred, and thousand years.
cards.remember_en: Four weeks is twenty-eight days; many months have extra days.

cards.question_en: Identify and sort polygons using sides and angles.
cards.idea_en: Identify and sort polygons using sides and angles.
steps_en: A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides.
Regular polygons have equal side lengths and equal corner angles.
This changed corner makes the pentagon irregular, though five sides remain.
cards.remember_en: Both conditions matter; equal sides alone are not enough.

cards.question_en: Complete reflected patterns with equal distances from a line.
cards.idea_en: Complete reflected patterns with equal distances from a line.
steps_en: A mirror line divides a picture into matching reflected halves.
Place each partner the same distance on the other side.
Folding along the line would place each shape over its partner.
cards.remember_en: Matching distances make the shapes overlap when folded.

cards.question_en: Follow and create routes using turns, distances, and facing.
cards.idea_en: Follow and create routes using turns, distances, and facing.
steps_en: If you face north, forward takes you towards north.
A quarter turn right changes your facing from north to east.
Say the turn and the distance so another person can follow.
cards.remember_en: Forward changes when your body or robot changes direction.

cards.question_en: Locate places using north, east, south, and west.
cards.idea_en: Locate places using north, east, south, and west.
steps_en: The north arrow fixes the directions on this simple map.
The pond is east of the tree on this map.
From the pond, travel west to return to the tree.
cards.remember_en: Reversing a trip reverses east and west.

cards.question_en: Choose questions, collect responses, and distinguish data types.
cards.idea_en: Choose questions, collect responses, and distinguish data types.
steps_en: Ask everyone the same question before recording their responses.
Repeated answers still count because they came from different people.
Pet counts are numbers; favourite pet types would be categories.
cards.remember_en: A pet count is a number; a favourite pet is a category.

cards.question_en: Represent complete data using frequencies, bars, and dots.
cards.idea_en: Represent complete data using frequencies, bars, and dots.
steps_en: Count each response to find the frequency for every category.
Each bar reaches the number of children in its category.
A dot plot uses one dot for each recorded response.
cards.remember_en: Height shows frequency using the graph’s scale.

cards.question_en: Read frequencies and answer questions about the measured group.
cards.idea_en: Read frequencies and answer questions about the measured group.
steps_en: Two children lost one tooth; three children lost two teeth.
Adding the bar heights counts six children in the survey.
Count teeth within each group, then combine all the groups.
cards.remember_en: Each child contributes two teeth, so three equal groups make six teeth.

connects_to.label_en: Year 4 · Describe what the data shows

cards.question_en: Read, write and compare whole numbers up to 10,000.
cards.idea_en: Read, write and compare whole numbers up to 10,000.
steps_en: Each column is ten times the column on its right.
Zero holds the hundreds place. The other digits keep their values.
3048 is greater than 2980 because three thousands exceeds two thousands.
cards.remember_en: The 3 is in the thousands column, so its value is 3000.

connects_to.label_en: Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Round whole numbers and tenths using neighbouring values.
cards.idea_en: Round whole numbers and tenths using neighbouring values.
steps_en: 364 lies between 300 and 400.
364 is nearer 400. The halfway point is 350.
cards.remember_en: 364 is 36 from 400 and 64 from 300.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · Round to a nearby ten or hundred

cards.question_en: Continue counting forwards or backwards in useful units.
cards.idea_en: Continue counting forwards or backwards in useful units.
steps_en: Start at 20. Each jump adds 5.
20, 25, 30, 35, 40 follow the same rule.
Counting backwards reverses the jumps: 40, 35, 30, 25, 20.
cards.remember_en: Reverse a +5 jump by subtracting 5.

cards.question_en: Add up to four-digit numbers using place value.
cards.idea_en: Add up to four-digit numbers using place value.
steps_en: In 2648 + 1375, ones sit under ones.
13 ones become 1 ten and 3 ones.
Regroup each column. 4023 − 1375 returns 2648.
cards.remember_en: Ten ones exchange for one ten without changing the total.

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Add and subtract large numbers

cards.question_en: Subtract up to four-digit numbers and check by addition.
cards.idea_en: Subtract up to four-digit numbers and check by addition.
steps_en: In 4023 − 1375, three ones are not enough for five.
Rename 4023 as 3 thousands, 9 hundreds, 11 tens and 13 ones.
2648 + 1375 = 4023, so the difference fits.
cards.remember_en: A thousand exchanged for hundreds still has the same value.

cards.question_en: Use multiplication and division facts from 2s to 10s.
cards.idea_en: Use multiplication and division facts from 2s to 10s.
steps_en: Four rows of six make 24.
24 shared into four equal rows gives six in each.
Ten times as many in each group gives 4 × 60 = 240.
cards.remember_en: Dividing by the number of groups finds six in each group.

cards.question_en: Multiply two- and three-digit numbers by one digit.
cards.idea_en: Multiply two- and three-digit numbers by one digit.
steps_en: Three groups of 124 contain hundreds, tens and ones.
Three groups give 300, 60 and 12.
300 + 60 + 12 = 372. Three groups of 124 fit.
cards.remember_en: Each of the three groups contains every part of 124.

cards.question_en: Divide up to three-digit numbers exactly by one digit.
cards.idea_en: Divide up to three-digit numbers exactly by one digit.
steps_en: Share 156 into three equal groups.
Each group has 52. Check: 52 × 3 = 156.
cards.remember_en: The two shared parts are 50 and 2, so each group has 52.

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Divide and use the remainder

cards.question_en: Connect tenths, fractions, decimals and multiplication by ten.
cards.idea_en: Connect tenths, fractions, decimals and multiplication by ten.
steps_en: One whole becomes ten tenths. Five tenths is one half.
13 tenths make 1 whole and 3 tenths: 1.3.
1.3 × 10 = 13. Every unit becomes ten times as large.
cards.remember_en: One half is five tenths: 5/10 = 0.5.

cards.question_en: Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator.
cards.idea_en: Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator.
steps_en: Compare parts of two equal-sized wholes.
Three fifths exceeds two fifths because the pieces have equal size.
With two pieces each, two thirds exceeds two fifths.
cards.remember_en: Thirds are larger pieces than fifths; both fractions take two pieces.

cards.question_en: Recognise equivalent fractions by repartitioning the same whole.
cards.idea_en: Recognise equivalent fractions by repartitioning the same whole.
steps_en: Shade one half of a whole.
Split each half into two equal parts. The shaded amount stays fixed.
1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 reach the same position.
cards.remember_en: The same shaded amount now covers two of the four equal parts.

cards.question_en: Locate mixed and improper fractions on a number line.
cards.idea_en: Locate mixed and improper fractions on a number line.
steps_en: Each whole contains four quarter-steps.
Seven quarters is one whole and three quarters.
7/4 and 1 3/4 name the same position.
cards.remember_en: Four quarters make one whole, leaving three quarters.

cards.question_en: Combine or remove equal fraction units, including beyond one whole.
cards.idea_en: Combine or remove equal fraction units, including beyond one whole.
steps_en: Three eighths and six eighths use equal-sized pieces.
3 + 6 makes 9 eighths, more than one whole.
Take away six eighths from nine eighths. Three eighths remain.
cards.remember_en: The equal-sized unit remains one eighth while the count changes.

cards.question_en: Add and subtract decimals to one decimal place.
cards.idea_en: Add and subtract decimals to one decimal place.
steps_en: 1.3 is thirteen tenths; 0.8 is eight tenths.
21 tenths make 2 wholes and 1 tenth.
2.1 − 0.8 = 1.3, so the total is consistent.
cards.remember_en: Twenty tenths make two wholes; one tenth remains.

cards.question_en: Scale quantities proportionally with multiplication and division.
cards.idea_en: Scale quantities proportionally with multiplication and division.
steps_en: One batch needs 30 g oats and 20 g fruit.
Double the recipe: 60 g oats and 40 g fruit.
Halving both doubled amounts returns the original batch.
cards.remember_en: Every ingredient uses the same scale factor.

cards.question_en: Find a unit fraction of a whole number with an integer result.
cards.idea_en: Find a unit fraction of a whole number with an integer result.
steps_en: 42 counters make one whole set.
Six equal groups contain seven counters each.
One sixth is seven. Six groups of seven rebuild 42.
cards.remember_en: Divide the whole set into six equal groups.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · Find one part of a quantity

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Several parts and the whole

cards.question_en: Find the whole from the amount in one equal part.
cards.idea_en: Find the whole from the amount in one equal part.
steps_en: One sixth of a ribbon is 7 cm. The whole has six parts.
Each of the six equal parts is 7 cm.
cards.remember_en: The whole has six equal parts, each seven centimetres.

cards.question_en: Represent currency with different denomination combinations.
cards.idea_en: Represent currency with different denomination combinations.
steps_en: One dollar is 100 cents.
Two $2 coins and one $1 coin make $5.
Five $1 coin make the same $5 total.
cards.remember_en: Each dollar is 100 cents, so two dollars is 200 cents.

cards.question_en: Calculate whole-dollar totals and change.
cards.idea_en: Calculate whole-dollar totals and change.
steps_en: Three notebooks cost $4 each.
The notebooks cost $12. Add a $5 pen: $17.
Pay $20. The $3 change and $17 cost rebuild $20.
cards.remember_en: Change is the amount between the cost and payment.

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Shop with dollars and cents

cards.question_en: Check and complete addition and subtraction number sentences.
cards.idea_en: Check and complete addition and subtraction number sentences.
steps_en: 460 + 140 and 600 have the same value.
Add 20 to both sides: 460 + 140 + 20 = 620.
If 460 + □ = 600, subtract 460 from both sides. The gap is 140.
cards.remember_en: Equal changes preserve equal amounts.

cards.question_en: Check and complete multiplication and division number sentences.
cards.idea_en: Check and complete multiplication and division number sentences.
steps_en: Four equal groups make 28.
28 divided equally into four groups gives 7.
Replace the box with seven. 4 × 7 = 28 is true.
cards.remember_en: Undo multiplying by four with division by four.

cards.question_en: Continue and create patterns using one constant operation.
cards.idea_en: Continue and create patterns using one constant operation.
steps_en: Two, four and six tiles grow by adding two each time.
3, 6, 12, 24 doubles each time. The added amount changes.
24, 12, 6, 3 follows the inverse rule: divide by two.
cards.remember_en: The same multiplication works for every neighbouring pair.

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Find and make a rule

cards.title_en: Choose a tool and a unit
cards.question_en: Choose tools and connect mixed length, mass and capacity units.
cards.idea_en: Choose tools and connect mixed length, mass and capacity units.
steps_en: One metre contains 100 centimetres.
1 m and 23 cm means 100 cm plus 23 cm.
A ruler measures length; a scale measures mass; a jug measures capacity.
cards.remember_en: A jug scale measures how much liquid a container can hold.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · Choose units and measure length

cards.question_en: Read temperature in degrees Celsius.
cards.idea_en: Read temperature in degrees Celsius.
steps_en: This thermometer marks every two degrees Celsius.
The liquid reaches halfway between 20 and 22: 21 °C.
26 °C is five degrees warmer than 21 °C.
cards.remember_en: The interval is two degrees, so halfway is one degree above 20.

connects_from.label_en: Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Add all outside edges to measure a polygon perimeter.
cards.idea_en: Add all outside edges to measure a polygon perimeter.
steps_en: Perimeter follows the outside edges once.
The four side lengths are 8, 5, 8 and 5 centimetres.
8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm. Two pairs give the same total.
cards.remember_en: Perimeter counts every outside edge once.

connects_from.label_en: Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Find rectangle area from rows and columns of square units.
cards.idea_en: Find rectangle area from rows and columns of square units.
steps_en: A rectangle has four rows of six square units.
Four rows of six give 4 × 6 = 24 square units.
If the area is 24 and one side is 6, the other side is 4.
cards.remember_en: There are four equal rows, each containing six square units.

connects_from.label_en: Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Measure irregular areas by combining squares and half squares.
cards.idea_en: Measure irregular areas by combining squares and half squares.
steps_en: Use identical square units, including cut half squares.
A triangular half-square has half the area of one square.
Six full squares and one half square cover 6 1/2 square units.
cards.remember_en: Two equal halves cover one whole square.

cards.question_en: Measure a cuboid volume by counting identical cubes.
cards.idea_en: Measure a cuboid volume by counting identical cubes.
steps_en: A layer has three cubes across and two cubes deep.
Two complete layers contain twelve cubes.
Every space is filled. Six cubes per layer times two layers gives twelve.
cards.remember_en: Volume includes all the filled three-dimensional space.

cards.question_en: Estimate angles using quarter, half and full turns.
cards.idea_en: Estimate angles using quarter, half and full turns.
steps_en: A quarter turn is 90 degrees: one right angle.
Two quarter turns make a half turn of 180 degrees.
Four right angles make 360 degrees, the turns around a rectangle.
cards.remember_en: Four quarters make one full turn of 360 degrees.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · Quarter, half, and full turns

cards.question_en: Read analogue and digital time to the nearest minute.
cards.idea_en: Read analogue and digital time to the nearest minute.
steps_en: Sixty minute marks go around once.
The hour hand is past nine. The minute hand points to seventeen.
The same morning time is 9:17 am.
cards.remember_en: The hour hand moves gradually as minutes pass.

cards.question_en: Convert and measure durations using the 60-based time system.
cards.idea_en: Convert and measure durations using the 60-based time system.
steps_en: One minute is sixty seconds; one hour is sixty minutes.
1 hour 42 minutes equals 60 + 42 = 102 minutes.
90 seconds equals one and a half minutes.
cards.remember_en: Time groups seconds and minutes in sixties.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · How long does it last?

cards.question_en: Classify regular and irregular polygons with up to twelve sides.
cards.idea_en: Classify regular and irregular polygons with up to twelve sides.
steps_en: A polygon closes using straight edges that meet at vertices.
A regular polygon has equal side lengths and equal interior angles.
Unequal sides or angles make a polygon irregular, not less of a polygon.
cards.remember_en: Both conditions must hold.

cards.question_en: Identify reflection symmetry, including infinitely many circle lines.
cards.idea_en: Identify reflection symmetry, including infinitely many circle lines.
steps_en: A mirror line makes matching halves, point for point.
A non-square rectangle has two mirror lines; a square has four.
A circle folds along any diameter. There are infinitely many directions.
cards.remember_en: Every diameter works, in any direction.

cards.question_en: Connect a cuboid with front, side and top views.
cards.idea_en: Connect a cuboid with front, side and top views.
steps_en: This cuboid is three cubes across, two deep and one high.
The front view has three columns and one row.
The top view has three columns and two rows of depth.
cards.remember_en: From directly above, width and depth remain visible.

cards.question_en: Perform and describe one-step transformations.
cards.idea_en: Perform and describe one-step transformations.
steps_en: A translation moves every point the same distance and direction.
A reflection places matching points equally far from the mirror line.
A rotation keeps one centre fixed while the shape turns.
cards.remember_en: A reflection makes a mirror image.

cards.question_en: Read and plot locations using row letters and column numbers.
cards.idea_en: Read and plot locations using row letters and column numbers.
steps_en: Letters name rows; numbers name columns on this map.
B3 is where row B meets column 3.
Move one square right from B3. The new square is B4.
cards.remember_en: Letters label rows; numbers label columns.

connects_from.label_en: Year 3 · Find places on a map

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Read and create a grid map

cards.question_en: Collect numerical data and distinguish categories, counts and measurements.
cards.idea_en: Collect numerical data and distinguish categories, counts and measurements.
steps_en: Pet type is a category; pet count is a counted number.
Leaf length is measured. Keep the unit with every value.
If recording whole centimetres, 6.2 rounds to 6 and 7.8 rounds to 8.
cards.remember_en: Length can lie between whole units and is read on a scale.

connects_from.label_en: Choose a tool and a unit

cards.question_en: Create a dot plot or bar graph with a clear title, labels and zero-based frequency.
cards.idea_en: Create a dot plot or bar graph with a clear title, labels and zero-based frequency.
steps_en: Our group recorded pet counts: 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4.
Repeated pet counts stack at the same value.
A bar graph shows the same frequencies. Its frequency scale starts at zero.
cards.remember_en: A dot stands for one observation; its position gives that value.

cards.question_en: Answer questions about people, data values and their frequencies.
cards.idea_en: Answer questions about people, data values and their frequencies.
steps_en: The horizontal position gives that person’s number of pets.
Three dots above 3 mean three people have three pets.
The most pets owned by one person is four, not the height of a stack.
cards.remember_en: The stack height counts people; the horizontal label counts pets.

cards.question_en: Describe patterns, middle groups and spread in a recorded data set.
cards.idea_en: Describe patterns, middle groups and spread in a recorded data set.
steps_en: The tallest stack shows a common value in this group.
The middle observation is 3; values spread from 1 to 4.
These seven observations describe our group, not every child in New Zealand.
cards.remember_en: The recorded group does not include every child, so the claim would go beyond the data.

connects_to.label_en: Year 5 · Read the story in the data

cards.question_en: Read, build and compare whole numbers up to one million.
cards.idea_en: Read, build and compare whole numbers up to one million.
steps_en: Each digit tells how many units belong in its place.
Ten units of one place make one unit of the next place.
Ten hundred-thousands make one million. The ten-to-one pattern continues.
cards.remember_en: That place contains 0 units of 10. 0 × 10 = 0.

connects_from.label_en: Year 4 · A digit needs a place

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · A place for every digit

cards.question_en: Use nearby benchmarks to round numbers and estimate totals.
cards.idea_en: Use nearby benchmarks to round numbers and estimate totals.
steps_en: 46,700 lies between two neighbouring thousands.
46,700 is closer to 47,000. Check the halfway point.
3.58 is beyond 3.5, so its nearest whole number is 4.
cards.remember_en: 2.37 lies between 2 and 3. The nearest whole number is 2.

cards.question_en: Keep a constant counting step and locate numbers below zero.
cards.idea_en: Keep a constant counting step and locate numbers below zero.
steps_en: Counting in twelves uses the same jump each time.
Zero is neither positive nor negative. Count one step at a time.
Negative temperatures lie below zero on a vertical scale.
cards.remember_en: The relationship is 33 + 22. 33 + 22 = 55.

cards.question_en: Use place value to add and subtract large whole numbers.
cards.idea_en: Use place value to add and subtract large whole numbers.
steps_en: Add units to units, tens to tens, and so on.
Fifteen ones become one ten and five ones.
2,468 plus 1,757 is 4,225. Subtract one addend to check.

cards.question_en: Use arrays and known facts to find products, quotients and factor pairs.
cards.idea_en: Use arrays and known facts to find products, quotients and factor pairs.
steps_en: Three rows of four show one factor pair of twelve.
Two rows of six make twelve too. Factors divide with no remainder.
Split twelve rows into ten rows and two more rows.
cards.remember_en: The relationship is 2 × 12. 2 × 12 = 24.

cards.question_en: Split factors by place value, then combine all partial products.
cards.idea_en: Split factors by place value, then combine all partial products.
steps_en: Split 23 into 20 and 3, and 14 into 10 and 4.
Each small rectangle holds one part of the full product.
All four rectangles together make 322. Nothing is left out.

cards.question_en: Find a quotient and remainder, then decide what the story needs.
cards.idea_en: Find a quotient and remainder, then decide what the story needs.
steps_en: Share twenty-three counters into groups of four.
Five complete groups use twenty counters. Three counters remain.
Twenty-three people need six four-seat boats, including one partly filled boat.
cards.remember_en: 2 × 117 + 1 = 235. The requested answer is 117.

cards.question_en: Represent and compare tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals.
cards.idea_en: Represent and compare tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals.
steps_en: The same whole is split into one hundred equal squares.
Thirty-five hundredths is three tenths and five hundredths.
0.35 is less than 0.40. The whole stays the same size.
cards.remember_en: 7 hundredths means 7 ÷ 100. The decimal is 0.07.

connects_to.label_en: Times ten, divided by one hundred

cards.title_en: Times ten, divided by one hundred
cards.question_en: Use place value to multiply or divide by 10 or 100.
cards.idea_en: Use place value to multiply or divide by 10 or 100.
steps_en: Three tenths and six hundredths make 0.36.
Multiplying by ten makes each digit count a unit ten times larger.
Dividing by one hundred splits each unit into one hundred equal parts.
cards.remember_en: The value becomes 100 times smaller. 7 ÷ 100 = 0.07.

cards.question_en: Rename equal amounts to compare fractions and connect mixed numbers.
cards.idea_en: Rename equal amounts to compare fractions and connect mixed numbers.
steps_en: Two thirds can be split into six ninths without changing the amount.
Six ninths is more than five ninths.
Five thirds fill one whole and two more thirds.
cards.remember_en: The denominator was multiplied by 2. The numerator is 1 × 2 = 2.

connects_to.label_en: Words and a scale for chance

cards.question_en: Match fraction units before adding or subtracting.
cards.idea_en: Match fraction units before adding or subtracting.
steps_en: We can join two thirds and one ninth after matching the part sizes.
Split each third into three ninths. Two thirds become six ninths.
Six ninths plus one ninth is seven ninths.

cards.question_en: Combine and remove hundredths while keeping place values aligned.
cards.idea_en: Combine and remove hundredths while keeping place values aligned.
steps_en: Forty-seven hundredths is 0.47.
Add twenty-eight hundredths to the forty-seven hundredths.
Seventy-five hundredths is 0.75. Subtracting 0.28 returns 0.47.
cards.remember_en: Think in hundredths: 127 + 18. The result is 1.45.

cards.question_en: Find one equal part to move between several parts and a whole.
cards.idea_en: Find one equal part to move between several parts and a whole.
steps_en: Thirty is the whole. We want three of its five equal parts.
Share thirty into five equal parts. Each part is six.
Three parts make eighteen. Reverse the steps to rebuild the whole.
cards.remember_en: One part is 9 ÷ 3 = 3. 3 × 2 = 6.

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · Several parts and the whole

cards.question_en: Connect common percentages with fractions, decimals, parts and wholes.
cards.idea_en: Connect common percentages with fractions, decimals, parts and wholes.
steps_en: Twenty-five percent is twenty-five of one hundred equal parts.
Twenty-five percent is one quarter. A quarter of forty is ten.
If a quarter is ten, all four quarters make forty.
cards.remember_en: Percent means out of 100, so 10% = 1/10 = 0.1. The matching choice is 1/10 and 0.1.

cards.question_en: Represent dollar amounts and calculate totals and change.
cards.idea_en: Represent dollar amounts and calculate totals and change.
steps_en: One dollar is one hundred cents. Keep both place-value units.
Five dollars seventy-five plus three dollars sixty makes nine dollars thirty-five.
From nine dollars thirty-five to ten dollars is sixty-five cents.
cards.remember_en: Use the stated dollar and cent values. The requested dollar amount is $3.59.

connects_from.label_en: Year 4 · Work out cost and change

cards.question_en: Compare expressions and find a missing number without changing equality.
cards.idea_en: Compare expressions and find a missing number without changing equality.
steps_en: Different expressions can name the same amount.
Removing the same amount from equal totals keeps them equal.
In 40 minus something equals 24, the missing amount is 16.

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · Equal or beyond the boundary

cards.question_en: Continue and explain a constant-change pattern, including decimals.
cards.idea_en: Continue and explain a constant-change pattern, including decimals.
steps_en: The numbers grow by one and a half each time.
Add one and a half to four and a half to reach six.
Some patterns multiply or divide by the same number each time.
cards.remember_en: Each change is 0.5. The next term is 3.

cards.question_en: Choose a tool, read its scale and record the measurement with units.
cards.idea_en: Choose a tool, read its scale and record the measurement with units.
steps_en: Check the units and labelled marks before measuring.
Four hundred millilitres split across eight spaces makes fifty per space.
Five spaces from zero give two hundred and fifty millilitres.
cards.remember_en: Each space is 1 cm. 0 + 1 × 1 = 1 cm.

cards.question_en: Express the same length in metres, centimetres or a mixed form.
cards.idea_en: Express the same length in metres, centimetres or a mixed form.
steps_en: One metre is the same length as one hundred centimetres.
Two metres and thirty-five centimetres is 235 centimetres, or 2.35 metres.
These relationships name the units. Our conversion practice uses metres and centimetres.
cards.remember_en: 123 cm = 1.23 m. The requested measurement is 1.23.

connects_from.label_en: Times ten, divided by one hundred
Year 4 · Choose a tool and a unit

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · Change the unit, keep the amount

cards.question_en: Find area and perimeter, then test whether one determines the other.
cards.idea_en: Find area and perimeter, then test whether one determines the other.
steps_en: Area counts square units. Perimeter measures the boundary.
Both shapes contain twelve squares, but their perimeters differ.
Both perimeters are sixteen. Their areas are twelve and fifteen.
cards.remember_en: The relationship is 3 × 5. 3 × 5 = 15.

cards.question_en: Combine whole and partial squares to estimate a region’s area.
cards.idea_en: Combine whole and partial squares to estimate a region’s area.
steps_en: A region can cover whole squares and only parts of others.
Two halves and four quarters each make one more square.
Three plus one plus one gives an estimated area of five square units.
cards.remember_en: Add 2 + 1/2 + 1/4. The estimated area is 11/4 square units.

cards.question_en: Find cuboid volume by counting cubes per layer and equal layers.
cards.idea_en: Find cuboid volume by counting cubes per layer and equal layers.
steps_en: Volume counts cubes filling the whole three-dimensional space.
Each layer has six cubes. There are three equal layers.
Three layers of six cubes make eighteen cubic centimetres.
cards.remember_en: The relationship is 6 × 2. 6 × 2 = 12.

connects_from.label_en: Year 4 · Fill a cuboid with cubes

cards.question_en: Use angle benchmarks to classify turns and construct angles up to 180°.
cards.idea_en: Use angle benchmarks to classify turns and construct angles up to 180°.
steps_en: A right angle is 90 degrees. Smaller turns are acute.
An obtuse angle lies between 90 and 180 degrees. A reflex angle exceeds 180.
Align the centre and zero line. Mark seventy degrees, then draw the second ray.
cards.remember_en: 30° is below 90°. The matching choice is Acute.

cards.question_en: Read clock times and calculate durations across hours and noon.
cards.idea_en: Read clock times and calculate durations across hours and noon.
steps_en: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand counts minutes.
Four forty-five in the afternoon is 16:45 in twenty-four-hour time.
Fifteen minutes to five, then twenty more, gives thirty-five minutes.
cards.remember_en: The long hand points to minute 13. The time is 1:13 p.m.

cards.question_en: Recognise line relationships in different orientations and polygons.
cards.idea_en: Recognise line relationships in different orientations and polygons.
steps_en: These straight lines stay the same distance apart and never meet.
These lines cross at a right angle, even when the picture is tilted.
A rectangle has parallel opposite sides and perpendicular adjacent sides.
cards.remember_en: Constant separation of 2 cm means the lines never meet. The matching choice is Parallel.

cards.question_en: Use matching ends and face connections to identify prisms and their nets.
cards.idea_en: Use matching ends and face connections to identify prisms and their nets.
steps_en: A prism has two identical parallel ends and flat faces.
A triangular prism has five faces, nine edges and six vertices.
Six connected squares can fold into a cube. Their positions matter.
cards.remember_en: 3 side faces and 2 ends. Total faces: 5.

cards.question_en: Describe a transformation using what changes and what stays the same.
cards.idea_en: Describe a transformation using what changes and what stays the same.
steps_en: A translation moves every point the same distance and direction.
A reflection makes a mirror image across a fixed line.
A rotation keeps one turning point fixed while the shape turns.
cards.remember_en: Every point moves the same distance and direction without turning. The matching choice is Translation.

cards.title_en: Read and create a grid map
cards.question_en: Use alphanumeric references and compass directions to follow and create routes.
cards.idea_en: Use alphanumeric references and compass directions to follow and create routes.
steps_en: A1 names a square: row A and column 1.
From A1, move two squares east and one south to B3.
From B3, go one square north and two west to reach A1.
cards.remember_en: The point lies in row A, column 1. The matching choice is A1.

cards.question_en: Record measurements consistently, then place each value in one clear group.
cards.idea_en: Record measurements consistently, then place each value in one clear group.
steps_en: Measure every object the same way. State the required rounding precision.
These six lengths are recorded to one decimal place.
Each measurement belongs in one range. Group counts still total six.
cards.remember_en: 1.03 cm is closest to 1 cm. Record 1 cm.

connects_to.label_en: Read the story in the data

cards.question_en: Keep paired categories together and compare their clustered bars.
cards.idea_en: Keep paired categories together and compare their clustered bars.
steps_en: Record group and travel choice on the same row for each child.
Count walking and riding separately for each group.
Place both groups side by side. A colour key identifies each group.
cards.remember_en: Walk bars are A=2, B=4; ride bars are A=1, B=4. The requested number is 2.

cards.title_en: Read the story in the data
cards.question_en: Use values, frequencies and context to explain what a data display supports.
cards.idea_en: Use values, frequencies and context to explain what a data display supports.
steps_en: A dot gives one recorded length. A stack shows how often it occurs.
Most records are near two centimetres. The middle records lie there too.
Lengths run from one to three centimetres. Do not invent unmeasured values.
cards.remember_en: The counts are 2, 5, and 3. The requested frequency is 5.

connects_from.label_en: Year 4 · Describe what the data shows

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · Read the story without overclaiming

cards.title_en: Words and a scale for chance
cards.question_en: Describe likelihood with words and place it between zero and one.
cards.idea_en: Describe likelihood with words and place it between zero and one.
steps_en: All ten counters are equally likely. Three are green and seven are gold.
Three tenths lies below one half, so green is unlikely.
Impossible is zero. Certain is one. All possible outcomes together make one.
cards.remember_en: 0 of 10 counters are red. The point is 0 on the 0–1 line.

connects_to.label_en: A chance model and an experiment

cards.title_en: A chance model and an experiment
cards.question_en: List simple outcomes and compare a fair model with repeated experimental results.
cards.idea_en: List simple outcomes and compare a fair model with repeated experimental results.
steps_en: One roll of a fair die can show any of these six equally likely outcomes.
The even event contains 2, 4 and 6: three of the six outcomes.
Twelve actual rolls could give eight even results. That does not change the fair-die model.
cards.remember_en: 12 total trials − 3 red outcomes. Blue occurred 9 times. This is a record, not a guaranteed next result.

connects_from.label_en: Words and a scale for chance

connects_to.label_en: Year 6 · Probability on a zero-to-one scale

cards.question_en: Read, build and compare whole numbers using groups of ten.
cards.idea_en: Read, build and compare whole numbers using groups of ten.
steps_en: Read large numbers in groups of three digits; adjacent digit places still have a tenfold relationship.
Ten equal units can be exchanged for one larger unit.
There is no final place: we can continue to larger or smaller units.
cards.remember_en: Every position to the left represents ten times as much.

cards.question_en: Find every positive factor pair for products of numbers from 1 to 12.
cards.idea_en: Find every positive factor pair for products of numbers from 1 to 12.
steps_en: Twelve counters fit in three equal rows of four.
The same twelve counters also make two rows of six.
A reversed pair does not make a new pair.
cards.remember_en: The next pairs are reversals of ones already listed.

cards.question_en: Recognise squares to 144 and cubes to 125 and connect their notation to arrays.
cards.idea_en: Recognise squares to 144 and cubes to 125 and connect their notation to arrays.
steps_en: Three rows of three make a square number.
A cube needs three equal dimensions.
Squared uses two equal factors. Cubed uses three.
cards.remember_en: Cubed means three equal factors, so it can count layers of a cube.

cards.question_en: Round whole numbers and hundredths, and use rounding to estimate calculations.
cards.idea_en: Round whole numbers and hundredths, and use rounding to estimate calculations.
steps_en: Place the number between neighbouring multiples of the rounding unit.
1260 is nearer 1300 than 1200.
1.26 is nearer 1.3 than 1.2.
cards.remember_en: 1300 + 2500 = 3800 is the requested estimate; it is not the exact sum.

cards.question_en: Count forwards and backwards across zero in temperature and balance situations.
cards.idea_en: Count forwards and backwards across zero in temperature and balance situations.
steps_en: Negative numbers lie left of zero; zero is neither positive nor negative.
On a thermometer, negative readings lie below zero.
Starting at negative four, move forwards six units to reach two.
cards.remember_en: Zero separates positive and negative values.

cards.question_en: Use brackets, powers and operation priorities, including left-to-right ties.
cards.idea_en: Use brackets, powers and operation priorities, including left-to-right ties.
steps_en: Brackets keep a sum together before multiplication.
Without brackets, multiply first, then add the separate amount.
Multiplication and division have equal priority.
cards.remember_en: Evaluate the power, then the multiplication, then the subtraction.

cards.question_en: Add and subtract using place value, regrouping and a reasonable check.
cards.idea_en: Add and subtract using place value, regrouping and a reasonable check.
steps_en: Line up ones with ones, tens with tens, and hundreds with hundreds.
Fourteen ones become one ten and four ones.
Subtraction can check an addition result.
cards.remember_en: Regrouping changes the representation, not the amount.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Add and subtract large numbers

cards.question_en: Split a two-digit factor into tens and ones and combine partial products.
cards.idea_en: Split a two-digit factor into tens and ones and combine partial products.
steps_en: Treat twelve as ten and two.
Multiply by the tens and by the ones.
The two partial products cover the whole rectangle.
cards.remember_en: Twenty and four combine to make twenty-four.

cards.question_en: Divide five-digit numbers by one digit and express remainders appropriately.
cards.idea_en: Divide five-digit numbers by one digit and express remainders appropriately.
steps_en: Thirty-one metres shared among six groups leaves one metre after five each.
One remaining metre split six ways adds one sixth to every share.
Objects may stay whole; lengths can use fractions; money may need rounding.
cards.remember_en: Five cars leave one person, so the context requires one additional whole car.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Divide and use the remainder

cards.question_en: Represent and compare decimals to thousandths and scale place values.
cards.idea_en: Represent and compare decimals to thousandths and scale place values.
steps_en: A tenth can be split into ten hundredths, then each hundredth into ten thousandths.
0.347 means three tenths, four hundredths and seven thousandths.
Multiplying by ten makes every digit worth ten times as much.
cards.remember_en: 0.47 is 470 thousandths, which is greater than 407 thousandths.

connects_to.label_en: Change the unit, keep the amount

cards.question_en: Use common units to compare fractions and move between mixed and improper forms.
cards.idea_en: Use common units to compare fractions and move between mixed and improper forms.
steps_en: One half and three sixths cover the same length.
Divide numerator and denominator by a common factor to simplify; compare using matching fractional units.
Seven thirds make two wholes and one third.
cards.remember_en: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor preserves the ratio.

connects_to.label_en: Add and subtract matching fraction units

cards.question_en: Connect common fractions with decimal and percentage representations.
cards.idea_en: Connect common fractions with decimal and percentage representations.
steps_en: A percentage tells how many parts out of one hundred.
Fifths connect quickly to tenths and percentages.
Thirty-one hundredths also means thirty-one percent.
cards.remember_en: Three quarters are seventy-five hundredths.

cards.title_en: Add and subtract matching fraction units
cards.question_en: Make equal fractional units before adding or subtracting fractions and mixed numbers.
cards.idea_en: Make equal fractional units before adding or subtracting fractions and mixed numbers.
steps_en: A half and a quarter use different part sizes.
Split each half in two to create quarters.
Two quarters and one quarter make three quarters.
cards.remember_en: Two quarters equal one half, so both fractional amounts can use quarters.

cards.question_en: Align decimal units and regroup without changing the amount.
cards.idea_en: Align decimal units and regroup without changing the amount.
steps_en: Keep ones, tenths, hundredths and thousandths in matching columns.
Thirteen thousandths become one hundredth and three thousandths.
Check a decimal addition by subtracting one part.
cards.remember_en: Write 2.400 if helpful: zeros keep the place-value columns visible.

cards.question_en: Find several equal parts, or rebuild the whole from a known collection of parts.
cards.idea_en: Find several equal parts, or rebuild the whole from a known collection of parts.
steps_en: Thirty-six counters are split into six equal parts.
Five sixths selects five of the six equal parts.
If five parts contain thirty, one part is six and the whole is thirty-six.
cards.remember_en: The known forty-five covers three equal parts, so divide by three.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Several parts and the whole

cards.question_en: Find common percentages and wholes, then maintain a proportion when comparing quantities.
cards.idea_en: Find common percentages and wholes, then maintain a proportion when comparing quantities.
steps_en: Twenty-five percent selects one quarter of a whole.
If twenty-five percent is fifteen, repeat that part four times.
Equivalent ratios keep the same fraction successful.
cards.remember_en: Twenty percent is one fifth of the whole.

cards.question_en: Calculate discounts and decide what a budget can afford.
cards.idea_en: Calculate discounts and decide what a budget can afford.
steps_en: One dollar is one hundred cents.
A twenty-five percent discount removes one quarter of the original price.
Subtract the discount, then compare the price with the available money.
cards.remember_en: Fifty percent is one half, and half of 120 is 60.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Shop with dollars and cents

cards.question_en: Check and complete number sentences with ≤ and ≥, respecting operation order.
cards.idea_en: Check and complete number sentences with ≤ and ≥, respecting operation order.
steps_en: Less than or equal to includes the boundary value.
Operations on each side must be completed before checking the relationship.
Undo an operation to find the largest or smallest permitted whole number.
cards.remember_en: Greater than or equal to includes equality.

cards.question_en: Describe a growing pattern rule and use it to predict and test later elements.
cards.idea_en: Describe a growing pattern rule and use it to predict and test later elements.
steps_en: Record each pattern position beside its number of tiles.
Each new position adds three tiles; two tiles stay as a fixed extra.
A rule predicts later values; substitute a position to check it.
cards.remember_en: Substituting each position checks both the increase and the fixed part.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Find and make a rule

cards.question_en: Locate and plot ordered pairs, including points on axes and values from rules.
cards.idea_en: Locate and plot ordered pairs, including points on axes and values from rules.
steps_en: The axes meet at the origin, written as (0, 0).
The first coordinate is horizontal; the second is vertical.
An axis point has zero for one coordinate.
cards.remember_en: Zero horizontal movement keeps the point on the vertical axis.

cards.title_en: Measure and estimate with a benchmark
cards.question_en: Choose and use tools and benchmarks for length, mass, capacity, temperature and duration.
cards.idea_en: Choose and use tools and benchmarks for length, mass, capacity, temperature and duration.
steps_en: An estimate uses a familiar measured amount as a reference.
Check the unit and the value of each scale interval.
A difference helps improve the next estimate; it is not evidence of failure.
cards.remember_en: If the object starts away from zero, subtract its starting reading from its ending reading.

cards.title_en: Change the unit, keep the amount
cards.question_en: Convert metric length, mass and capacity, including mixed units to two decimal places.
cards.idea_en: Convert metric length, mass and capacity, including mixed units to two decimal places.
steps_en: Centi means one hundredth; milli means one thousandth; kilo means one thousand.
One kilogram contains one thousand grams.
Express both parts in the same unit before combining them.
cards.remember_en: One litre is 1000 millilitres, so multiply 1.25 by 1000.

cards.question_en: Use square units and a rectangle to calculate and compare right-triangle areas.
cards.idea_en: Use square units and a rectangle to calculate and compare right-triangle areas.
steps_en: A rectangle has equal rows of square units.
A diagonal divides the rectangle into two equal-area right triangles.
Use perpendicular base and height, then divide by two.
cards.remember_en: The perpendicular base and height match the sides of the enclosing rectangle.

cards.question_en: Calculate and compare volume as the count of unit cubes in equal layers.
cards.idea_en: Calculate and compare volume as the count of unit cubes in equal layers.
steps_en: A layer has length times width unit cubes.
Multiply the base layer count by the number of layers.
Two layers of twelve cubes make twenty-four cubic centimetres.
cards.remember_en: Multiply that fifteen-cube layer by two layers to find the volume.

cards.question_en: Measure and construct angles, then use full turns, straight lines and opposite angles to reason.
cards.idea_en: Measure and construct angles, then use full turns, straight lines and opposite angles to reason.
steps_en: Angles sharing a straight line add to one hundred and eighty degrees.
All angles around one point add to three hundred and sixty degrees.
When straight lines cross, vertically opposite angles are equal.
cards.remember_en: A reflex angle is greater than 180° but less than 360°.

cards.question_en: Convert time units and find durations using 12- and 24-hour times and timetables.
cards.idea_en: Convert time units and find durations using 12- and 24-hour times and timetables.
steps_en: Two fifty-three in the afternoon is 14:53 in the 24-hour system.
Count seven minutes to 15:00, then twenty-eight more to 15:28.
A timetable pairs events with times; calculate the interval you actually need.
cards.remember_en: Ten minutes reaches noon, then fifteen more gives twenty-five minutes.

cards.question_en: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by sides and angles, allowing overlapping families.
cards.idea_en: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by sides and angles, allowing overlapping families.
steps_en: A tilted square still has four equal sides and four right angles.
A square is also a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram.
A diagonal divides a quadrilateral into two triangles.
cards.remember_en: A shape can belong to several families when it meets all their definitions.

cards.question_en: Compare faces, bases and vertices of prisms and pyramids.
cards.idea_en: Compare faces, bases and vertices of prisms and pyramids.
steps_en: Two matching parallel bases are joined by side faces.
One base joins to triangular side faces meeting at a single apex.
The number of base sides predicts the side-face count.
cards.remember_en: A pyramid’s side triangles share one apex; a prism has a second matching base.

cards.question_en: Find rotational order and smallest matching turns, including a circle’s infinite order.
cards.idea_en: Find rotational order and smallest matching turns, including a circle’s infinite order.
steps_en: Count matches during one full turn, without counting the start twice.
A square matches four times in a full turn, so its order is four.
An unmarked circle has infinitely many matching turns.
cards.remember_en: It matches after a half-turn and a full turn, but not a quarter-turn.

cards.question_en: Create tessellations and explain how transformations preserve the tiles.
cards.idea_en: Create tessellations and explain how transformations preserve the tiles.
steps_en: A tessellation covers a surface with repeated shapes.
Triangles can fit together as paired halves of rectangles.
Angles around each meeting point must total a full turn.
cards.remember_en: A translation moves a shape without resizing it or changing its angles.

cards.question_en: Predict two successive reflections, translations or rotations and track a shape.
cards.idea_en: Predict two successive reflections, translations or rotations and track a shape.
steps_en: Keep the transformation line, centre or movement clearly marked.
Reflecting in the vertical axis changes right to left.
Moving three right takes the reflected point to one, one.
cards.remember_en: A translation is a slide; reflection is a flip and rotation is a turn.

connects_to.label_en: Year 7 · Move a shape on a grid

cards.question_en: Use labelled map squares, simple scales, compass points and turns to describe a route.
cards.idea_en: Use labelled map squares, simple scales, compass points and turns to describe a route.
steps_en: Letters name rows and numbers name columns in this map.
One centimetre can stand for a larger real distance.
A route needs direction, distance and any turn at a corner.
cards.remember_en: East changes the column number; the row stays the same.

connects_from.label_en: Change the unit, keep the amount
Year 5 · Read and create a grid map

cards.question_en: Collect paired time measurements and choose and create a suitable graph.
cards.idea_en: Collect paired time measurements and choose and create a suitable graph.
steps_en: Each row pairs a time with one measured value.
Time is horizontal; the measured variable is vertical.
Different subjects or times can give different answers.
cards.remember_en: A time-series observation pairs a time with the measurement made then.

connects_from.label_en: Measure and estimate with a benchmark

cards.question_en: Calculate and interpret means and ranges for numerical and continuous data.
cards.idea_en: Calculate and interpret means and ranges for numerical and continuous data.
steps_en: The mean is the total shared across the number of observations.
Rearranging the same total can show the mean without changing the total.
The range is the distance from the lowest value to the highest.
cards.remember_en: Add all measurements and divide by their count; the range uses maximum minus minimum.

cards.question_en: Describe graph variables, units, shape, centre, spread and trends without inventing causes.
cards.idea_en: Describe graph variables, units, shape, centre, spread and trends without inventing causes.
steps_en: Identify the variable, unit, time span and scale before interpreting a graph.
An overall rise can still contain a dip.
A graph describes observed values; it does not by itself prove a cause.
cards.remember_en: A time sequence alone does not establish a cause or guarantee a future value.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · Read the story in the data

cards.question_en: List possible outcomes and group them into events for a single chance trial.
cards.idea_en: List possible outcomes and group them into events for a single chance trial.
steps_en: A chance trial produces one result from a set of possible outcomes.
The sample space lists every possible label, without repetition.
The event “even” includes two, four and six.
cards.remember_en: An even-number event groups 2, 4 and 6. Rolling 4 is also an event, but it contains only one outcome.

cards.question_en: Calculate probabilities for fair equal-sector spinners and locate them on a likelihood scale.
cards.idea_en: Calculate probabilities for fair equal-sector spinners and locate them on a likelihood scale.
steps_en: For a fair spinner, count favourable equal sectors over all sectors.
Gold covers three of eight equally likely outcomes.
Three eighths lies below one half: gold is less likely than not gold.
cards.remember_en: Counting sectors assumes equal areas and a fair spinning mechanism.

connects_from.label_en: Year 5 · A chance model and an experiment

connects_to.label_en: Combine outcomes and check the whole

cards.title_en: Combine outcomes and check the whole
cards.question_en: Combine disjoint outcomes and use total probability one to find missing chances.
cards.idea_en: Combine disjoint outcomes and use total probability one to find missing chances.
steps_en: On one spin, red or blue includes either colour.
Disjoint events cannot happen together in one trial, so their probabilities can be added.
The selected event and everything else together exhaust all possible outcomes.
cards.remember_en: An event and its complement exhaust the outcomes: one minus three fifths equals two fifths.

cards.question_en: Read powers and build large numbers.
cards.idea_en: Read powers and build large numbers.
steps_en: Place values continue in both directions; each leftward step multiplies by ten.
3³ means three factors of 3, giving 27.
Keep zeros for empty places: 34,506 = 3×10⁴ + 4×10³ + 5×10² + 6.
cards.remember_en: Multiply 10 by itself the stated number of times. Answer: 100.

connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · A place for every digit

connects_to.label_en: Year 8 · Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Use factors to recognise number structure.
cards.idea_en: Use factors to recognise number structure.
steps_en: A 12 by 12 square has 144 cells. So √144 = 12.
Seven dots make only 1×7 and 7×1 rectangles. Seven is prime; one is neither.
Use last digits for 2, 4, 5, 8, 10; digit sums for 3, 9; both 2 and 3 for 6.

cards.question_en: Choose HCF for groups and LCM for repeats.
cards.idea_en: Choose HCF for groups and LCM for repeats.
steps_en: Twelve and eighteen counters can each be arranged in groups of six.
Six is the largest factor appearing in both lists.
Multiples of 4 and 6 first meet at 12. LCM(4,6) = 12.
cards.remember_en: Choose the greatest shared factor. Answer: 4.

cards.question_en: Use direction and zero to work with integers.
cards.idea_en: Use direction and zero to work with integers.
steps_en: Integers continue without end. Negative integers lie left of zero.
−4 and 4 are the same distance from zero; together they give zero.
Start at −3. Adding 5 moves right to 2; subtracting 5 moves left.

connects_to.label_en: Year 8 · Signed numbers on a line

cards.question_en: Calculate carefully and check the size of answers.
cards.idea_en: Calculate carefully and check the size of answers.
steps_en: 3,460 is 60 above 3,400 and 40 below 3,500; it rounds to 3,500.
327 ÷ 5 = 65 + 2/5 = 65.4. The two remaining units are shared equally.
cards.remember_en: Use the next digit: 5 or more rounds up. Answer: 25000.

cards.question_en: Use brackets, powers and equal-priority operations.
cards.idea_en: Use brackets, powers and equal-priority operations.
steps_en: 3 + 2 × 4 has two groups of four, then three extra.
(3 + 2) × 4 has five groups of four, giving twenty.
12 ÷ 3 × 2 means divide twelve into three groups, then double four.
cards.remember_en: Multiply first: 4 × 4 = 16; then add 3. Answer: 19.

cards.question_en: Connect equivalent fractions, decimals and percentages.
cards.idea_en: Connect equivalent fractions, decimals and percentages.
steps_en: 1/2, 2/4 and 50% describe the same half of one whole.
3/4 is 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. This decimal ends; 1/3 = 0.333… does not.
3/5 = 6/10 = 60%. There are infinitely many equivalent names at the same point.
cards.remember_en: Divide numerator and denominator by 2. Answer: 3/5.

cards.question_en: Use a common unit, then simplify.
cards.idea_en: Use a common unit, then simplify.
steps_en: One half and one third use different-sized pieces of the same whole.
1/2 becomes 3/6; 1/3 becomes 2/6. Add five equal pieces.
cards.remember_en: Use denominator 6: 1/6 = 1/6; 1/2 = 3/6. Answer: 2/3.

cards.question_en: Find a part, share it, or rebuild the whole.
cards.idea_en: Find a part, share it, or rebuild the whole.
steps_en: 3/4 of 20 is three groups of five: 15.
Share 3/4 equally among three people. Each person receives 1/4.
If 3/4 is 15, one quarter is 5 and the whole is 20.

connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · Several parts and the whole

cards.question_en: Keep place values aligned as quantities change.
cards.idea_en: Keep place values aligned as quantities change.
steps_en: 0.4 + 0.3 combines four tenths and three tenths into seven tenths.
Multiplying by ten makes each digit worth ten times as much.
0.7 × 5 is 7 tenths × 5 = 35 tenths = 3.5.
cards.remember_en: Align decimal points so hundredths add to hundredths. Answer: 1.87.

cards.question_en: Scale each part with the same multiplier.
cards.idea_en: Scale each part with the same multiplier.
steps_en: 25% means one quarter: 25 out of every 100 equal parts.
If 40% is 28, each 20% is 14. Five equal parts make 100% = 70.
3 red for 7 blue: six groups give 18 red and 42 blue, 60 beads altogether.

cards.question_en: Find totals, discounts and cash change.
cards.idea_en: Find totals, discounts and cash change.
steps_en: A $12.35 item and a $7.48 item total $19.83.
Electronic payment stays $19.83; cash rounds the final total to $19.80.
On a $60 price, 20% is $12. The sale price is $48.

cards.question_en: Undo operations and check the solution.
cards.idea_en: Undo operations and check the solution.
steps_en: Two unknown bags and three counters balance eleven counters: 2x + 3 = 11.
Remove three counters from both sides. Now 2x = 8.
Split eight into two equal groups: x = 4. Check: 2×4 + 3 = 11.
cards.remember_en: Subtract 3 from both sides. Substitute x = 3 into the original equation to check. Answer: 3.
