connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · Equal or beyond the boundary

cards.question_en: Read compact notation and rearrange formulas.
cards.idea_en: Read compact notation and rearrange formulas.
steps_en: 3a + 2a has five copies of a. Unlike quantities cannot be joined this way.
For a = 4, a² is a×a = 16. A square gives the product meaning.
A = lw. Dividing by l gives w = A/l; 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

cards.question_en: Read and plot ordered pairs across both axes.
cards.idea_en: Read and plot ordered pairs across both axes.
steps_en: The axes meet at (0,0). Read across first, then up or down.
(−3,2) is left and up. (2,−3) is right and down.
Each row makes one point. Keep the first number horizontal.
cards.remember_en: The x-coordinate is 2. Answer: 2.

connects_to.label_en: Move a shape on a grid

cards.question_en: Connect growing diagrams, tables, rules and lines.
cards.idea_en: Connect growing diagrams, tables, rules and lines.
steps_en: One square needs four sticks. Each joined square adds three more.
Term n has 3n + 1 sticks. The extra one is there before the repeats.
For y = x + 1, every step right adds one up; the plotted points lie on a line.
cards.remember_en: 6 − 4 = 2. Answer: 2.

cards.question_en: Match a measure and prefix to the object.
cards.idea_en: Match a measure and prefix to the object.
steps_en: A centimetre is one hundredth of a metre. Ten centimetres fit into each marked section.
One kilogram has the same mass as 1000 grams.
Four 250 mL portions fill one litre.

connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · Change the unit, keep the amount

connects_to.label_en: Year 8 · Square units, cube units, water

cards.question_en: Use the outside boundary to find missing lengths.
cards.idea_en: Use the outside boundary to find missing lengths.
steps_en: A 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle has two sides of each length.
For P = 22 and l = 7, half the perimeter is 11. Width = 11 − 7 = 4.
Trace every outside segment once; inner cutting lines are not part of the perimeter.

cards.question_en: Use square units and perpendicular heights.
cards.idea_en: Use square units and perpendicular heights.
steps_en: A 6 by 4 rectangle contains 24 unit squares; its area is 24 cm².
A diagonal splits the rectangle into two equal triangles: 6×4÷2 = 12 cm².
A rectangle and a triangle can share a base; add their areas without counting overlap.

cards.question_en: Count three dimensions and recover missing lengths.
cards.idea_en: Count three dimensions and recover missing lengths.
steps_en: A 4 by 3 base contains 12 cubes per layer.
Two layers of twelve cubes make 24 cubic units: V = lwh.
With volume 60 cm³ and base area 20 cm², height is 60 ÷ 20 = 3 cm.

cards.question_en: Cross hours and midnight without losing minutes.
cards.idea_en: Cross hours and midnight without losing minutes.
steps_en: One hour has four quarters. Each quarter is 15 minutes.
The 09:45 train arrives at 11:10; count 15 + 60 + 10 = 85 minutes.
Arrive 11:10, then depart 11:35: the connection adds 25 minutes.

connects_to.label_en: Year 8 · Time across hours and days

cards.question_en: Use side properties and angle properties together.
cards.idea_en: Use side properties and angle properties together.
steps_en: Two equal sides give equal base angles. Isosceles means at least two equal sides.
This triangle has a right angle; its three unequal sides make it scalene.
An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles. It is acute and also isosceles.
cards.remember_en: Every angle is smaller than 90°. Choose: Acute.

cards.question_en: Use turns, lines and polygons to solve angles.
cards.idea_en: Use turns, lines and polygons to solve angles.
steps_en: Walking around a polygon turns you once. A regular square has four equal 90° exterior turns.
A quadrilateral splits into two triangles: 2×180° = 360°. In general, use 180(n−2).
Corresponding angles are equal. Vertical angles are equal; adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°.

connects_to.label_en: Year 8 · Polygon angles and a proof

cards.title_en: Move a shape on a grid
cards.question_en: Translate, reflect and rotate with a stated rule.
cards.idea_en: Translate, reflect and rotate with a stated rule.
steps_en: A translation adds the same vector to every vertex; here, move two right and one up.
A(−3,2) and A′(3,2) are equally far from the y-axis on opposite sides.
A 90° anticlockwise turn about the origin sends (3,1) to (−1,3).
cards.remember_en: 1 + 3 = 4. Answer: 4.

cards.question_en: Match flat faces to prisms and pyramids.
cards.idea_en: Match flat faces to prisms and pyramids.
steps_en: A net places all six faces flat. Their edges must meet without overlap when folded.
A triangular prism has two triangles and three rectangles. Attach ends along matching edges.
A square pyramid net has a square base and four congruent triangular sides.
cards.remember_en: 4 base edges give 4 rectangular faces. Answer: 4.

cards.question_en: Describe where to move using directions and angles.
cards.idea_en: Describe where to move using directions and angles.
steps_en: Halfway between north and east is northeast: 45° east from north.
From (−2,−1), three east and two north reach (1,1).
State a start, direction, distance and turn. A quarter-turn clockwise is 90°.

cards.question_en: Choose a variable, group and consistent method.
cards.idea_en: Choose a variable, group and consistent method.
steps_en: Categories name groups; discrete numbers count; continuous numbers measure.
“How do our foot lengths vary?” expects different lengths, measured with one method and unit.
Each row is one person. Record the unit and who was measured; avoid unnecessary names.
cards.remember_en: This groups responses into named categories. Choose: Categorical.

cards.question_en: Choose and calculate a useful centre.
cards.idea_en: Choose and calculate a useful centre.
steps_en: The values 2, 4 and 6 share twelve units equally. The mean is four.
Sort 8, 3, 6, 4, 7 into 3, 4, 6, 7, 8. The median is 6.
The mode can be a category: walk is the most common travel method.
cards.remember_en: Total 24 ÷ count 4 = 6. Answer: 6.

cards.question_en: Use range and investigate outliers carefully.
cards.idea_en: Use range and investigate outliers carefully.
steps_en: For 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, the range is 8 − 4 = 4.
Replacing 8 with 30 changes the range to 26; most values are still near 6.
For these five values, the median stays 6; the mean rises from 6 to 10.4.
cards.remember_en: 9 − 2 = 7. Answer: 7.

cards.question_en: Read and build graphs that show frequencies.
cards.idea_en: Read and build graphs that show frequencies.
steps_en: Each dot represents one pupil. Keep category labels clear.
A zero baseline and equal-width bars help viewers compare frequencies.
A graph needs a group, variable, and frequency scale; these are ten pupils’ travel methods.
cards.remember_en: The bus bar reaches 4 pupils. Answer: 4.

cards.question_en: Choose graphs that preserve the relationship.
cards.idea_en: Choose graphs that preserve the relationship.
steps_en: Travel method and class are two categorical variables. Clustered bars compare classes within each travel category.
Stacking preserves both class counts and each travel method’s total; the legend names the groups.
A time-series graph pairs each time with a measurement; join points in time order.
cards.remember_en: The Class B bus bar is 5. Answer: 5.

cards.question_en: Use shape, centre, spread and context together.
cards.idea_en: Use shape, centre, spread and context together.
steps_en: This distribution has one central peak and roughly matching sides: approximately symmetrical.
A right tail extends toward high values: positive skew. A left tail gives negative skew.
For these five wait times, median = 3 minutes and range = 8 minutes. Most waits are short.
cards.remember_en: Frequencies rise and fall at similar rates on both sides of the centre. Choose: Approximately symmetrical.

cards.question_en: Check labels, scales and evidence before concluding.
cards.idea_en: Check labels, scales and evidence before concluding.
steps_en: Values 48 and 50 differ by two. Bars starting at 47 can exaggerate their apparent size difference.
A zero baseline makes the same difference clear without enlarging it visually.
Without a labelled vertical scale, these heights cannot tell us exact quantities.
cards.remember_en: Without a vertical label, height might mean a count, percentage, or measurement. Choose: What the height measures and its unit.

connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · Read the story without overclaiming

cards.question_en: Use lists, tables and trees without missing cases.
cards.idea_en: Use lists, tables and trees without missing cases.
steps_en: A coin outcome pairs with a colour. The tree lists HR, HB, TR and TB without missing a pair.
Two coin outcomes paired with three spinner numbers make six ordered outcomes.
The event “heads” contains H1, H2 and H3: three of the six possible ordered outcomes.
cards.remember_en: 2 × 3 = 6. Answer: 6.

cards.question_en: Count equally likely outcomes and compare chances.
cards.idea_en: Count equally likely outcomes and compare chances.
steps_en: Three red counters among ten identical counters give P(red) = 3/10.
Seven counters are not red. P(not red) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10.
A larger probability lies farther right; 7/10 is more likely than 3/10.
cards.remember_en: P(red) = 3/10. Answer: 3/10.

connects_from.label_en: Year 6 · Probability on a zero-to-one scale

cards.question_en: Estimate chance from recorded outcomes.
cards.idea_en: Estimate chance from recorded outcomes.
steps_en: In one set of 30 coin tosses, 17 are heads and 13 tails. These are observations, not a rule.
Experimental P(heads) is 17/30. A fair-coin model gives theoretical P(heads) = 1/2.
The second group gets 14 heads in 30 trials. Random variation makes different results possible.

cards.question_en: Compare every outcome with a theoretical model.
cards.idea_en: Compare every outcome with a theoretical model.
steps_en: In this example, 54 heads and 46 tails occur in 100 fair-coin trials.
The experimental values 0.54 and 0.46 are each 0.04 from the fair model’s 0.5.
For a stable fair process, long-run relative frequencies approach 0.5; individual steps can move away.

cards.title_en: Powers on both sides of one
cards.question_en: Read, build, and order numbers with powers of ten.
cards.idea_en: Read, build, and order numbers with powers of ten.
steps_en: Moving right divides each place value by ten. The pattern continues beyond either edge.
The digits name hundreds, ones, tenths, and hundredths.
Expand the number. A negative power describes a fraction of one.
cards.remember_en: Divide 1 by 100. The answer is 1/100.

cards.question_en: Split composites into primes; undo squares and cubes.
cards.idea_en: Split composites into primes; undo squares and cubes.
steps_en: Split 72 into factors; keep splitting composite branches.
The prime factors are unique, apart from their order. Exponents count repeated factors.
The square shows √16 = 4: a square root finds the side. A cube root finds a cube edge, so ∛125 = 5.
cards.remember_en: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. The answer is 2.

connects_from.label_en: Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Locate, compare, add, and subtract signed numbers.
cards.idea_en: Locate, compare, add, and subtract signed numbers.
steps_en: Integers include negative whole numbers, zero, and positive whole numbers. The line continues both ways.
Start at −3. Adding 5 moves five steps right.
Opposite numbers add to zero. Subtracting a negative moves right.
cards.remember_en: Start at −4; move 3 places right. The answer is -1.

connects_from.label_en: Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Bound an answer and explain its remainder.
cards.idea_en: Bound an answer and explain its remainder.
steps_en: 14.7 lies between 14 and 15, so its product by 5 lies between 70 and 75.
327 ÷ 15 gives 21 whole groups and 12 left. Share the remainder too.
12/15 = 0.8, so 327 ÷ 15 = 21.8. Multiply back to check.
cards.remember_en: 14815 is between 14800 and 14900. The nearer multiple is 14800.

connects_from.label_en: Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Use groups, powers, and equal-rank operations correctly.
cards.idea_en: Use groups, powers, and equal-rank operations correctly.
steps_en: Use GEMA: grouped, exponents, multiplicative, additive. Brackets come first.
Squaring creates a 3-by-3 array. Finish the power before adding or subtracting.
Multiplication and division share rank. Addition and subtraction also share rank.
cards.remember_en: First multiply 3 × 3. The answer is 8.

cards.question_en: Rename and compare the same proportion.
cards.idea_en: Rename and compare the same proportion.
steps_en: One whole is split into four equal parts. Three parts are shaded.
Each quarter is 25 hundredths. Three quarters make 75 hundredths.
Fraction, decimal, and percentage describe the same proportion of the same whole.
cards.remember_en: Multiply 3/20 by 100. The answer is 15.

connects_from.label_en: Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Multiply fractions and find a whole from one part.
cards.idea_en: Multiply fractions and find a whole from one part.
steps_en: Shade two thirds of one whole.
Take three quarters of the shaded amount. Multiply both numerators and both denominators.
Six of twelve equal cells overlap: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.
cards.remember_en: 1 × 2 = 2 and 2 × 3 = 6; then cancel common factors. The answer is 1/3.

cards.question_en: Multiply decimals and scale by powers of ten.
cards.idea_en: Multiply decimals and scale by powers of ten.
steps_en: Multiplying by ten makes every digit’s value ten times larger.
2.4 is 24 tenths. Three copies contain 72 tenths.
cards.remember_en: Multiply the value by 10. The answer is 20.

connects_from.label_en: Powers on both sides of one

cards.question_en: Find a percentage, recover 100%, and change an amount.
cards.idea_en: Find a percentage, recover 100%, and change an amount.
steps_en: 20% means 20 out of every 100: one fifth of the whole.
If 20% is 16, five equal parts make the whole.
A 20% increase keeps the original 100% and adds 20%.

cards.question_en: Split a whole using part:part and part:whole ratios.
cards.idea_en: Split a whole using part:part and part:whole ratios.
steps_en: Red:blue = 2:3. The whole has five equal ratio parts.
A total of 40 shared across five parts gives 8 in each part.
Red is 2/5 of the whole, or 40%. Part:part and part:whole ratios differ.
cards.remember_en: 6 parts share 30; each part is 5. The answer is 10.

cards.question_en: Apply a discount and round the right total.
cards.idea_en: Apply a discount and round the right total.
steps_en: A 25% discount saves one quarter. Pay the other three quarters.
75% of $80 is $60. Round calculated currency amounts to cents.
For cash, round the final bill to the nearest 10 cents. Card totals stay in cents.
cards.remember_en: Keep 85% of $100. The answer is 85.

cards.question_en: Build and compare weekly, monthly, and yearly plans.
cards.idea_en: Build and compare weekly, monthly, and yearly plans.
steps_en: Use 52 weeks or 12 calendar months for a yearly comparison; a month is not exactly four weeks.
Four payments can still include fees. Add all fees to the item price.
Income minus all spending gives savings. Compare costs and benefits before choosing.
cards.remember_en: 7 × 52. The answer is 364.

cards.question_en: Form and solve linear equations with rational answers.
cards.idea_en: Form and solve linear equations with rational answers.
steps_en: A variable can name a changing quantity or an unknown. Here x is an unknown equal piece.
Subtract 6 from both sides to keep the equation balanced.
Divide both sides by 3. Check: 3 × 4 + 6 = 18; trial and error is less efficient here.
cards.remember_en: 3 × (−1) − 4. The answer is -7.

cards.question_en: Solve an inequality and show its solution set.
cards.idea_en: Solve an inequality and show its solution set.
steps_en: x ≥ −2 includes −2 and every larger number. Use a filled endpoint.
x < 2 excludes the boundary. Use an open endpoint and shade left.
For x + 3 ≥ 1, subtract 3: x ≥ −2. Dividing by a negative reverses the inequality.
cards.remember_en: x ≥ 5 − 4 = 1. The endpoint is included; shade right.

cards.question_en: Use algebraic laws to rewrite equal expressions.
cards.idea_en: Use algebraic laws to rewrite equal expressions.
steps_en: Two rows of x + 3 tiles give 2(x + 3). The bracket names one row.
Distribute 2 to both terms: 2x + 6. Like terms may be reordered and regrouped.
Factorising extracts a common factor. Expanded and factorised expressions keep the same value.
cards.remember_en: Add their coefficients: 3 + 5. The answer is 8.

cards.question_en: Undo one or two steps to make a new subject.
cards.idea_en: Undo one or two steps to make a new subject.
steps_en: The formula y = 3x + 4 multiplies first and then adds.
Remove 4 before dividing by 3. Apply each operation to both sides.
x = (y − 4)/3 works for every row. Substitution checks the result.

cards.question_en: Use tables and graphs to explain a constant change.
cards.idea_en: Use tables and graphs to explain a constant change.
steps_en: The four quadrants meet at (0, 0). Read x first, then y.
The rule t = 2n + 1 adds two for each step. It also predicts earlier and later values.
The plotted points lie on one straight line because the increase is constant.
cards.remember_en: 2 × 6 + 2. The answer is 14.

cards.question_en: Build, extend, table, and plot figurate patterns.
cards.idea_en: Build, extend, table, and plot figurate patterns.
steps_en: Each new triangular term adds a longer row.
Squares and cubes use repeated multiplication. Their increases change with n.
Use position as x and the term as y. Curving patterns are not linear.
cards.remember_en: 4 × 5 ÷ 2. The answer is 10.

cards.question_en: Measure carefully and convert area, volume, and capacity.
cards.idea_en: Measure carefully and convert area, volume, and capacity.
steps_en: A square centimetre contains 10 rows of 10 square millimetres.
A cubic centimetre contains 10 × 10 × 10 cubic millimetres.
1 mL = 1 cm³; 1 L = 1000 cm³; 1 m³ = 1000 L.
cards.remember_en: 1 cm² = 10 × 10 = 100 mm². The answer is 300.

cards.question_en: Use perpendicular height in area formulas.
cards.idea_en: Use perpendicular height in area formulas.
steps_en: The height meets the base at a right angle. A sloping edge is different.
Move the end triangle to make a rectangle: A = base × height.
A trapezium has area (a + b)h/2. Here (6 + 10) × 4/2 = 32.
cards.remember_en: Area = base × perpendicular height. The answer is 24.

cards.question_en: Link perimeter, area, and missing dimensions.
cards.idea_en: Link perimeter, area, and missing dimensions.
steps_en: For a rectangle, half its perimeter is length plus width.
Width = 15 − 9 = 6. Now both dimensions are known.
Area = 9 × 6 = 54. Check the perimeter: 2(9 + 6) = 30.
cards.remember_en: Width = 24/2 − 8 = 4; area = 8 × 4. The answer is 32.

cards.question_en: Multiply cross-section area by length; combine volumes.
cards.idea_en: Multiply cross-section area by length; combine volumes.
steps_en: A triangular prism repeats one triangle along its length.
The triangle area is half the base times its perpendicular height.
Volume is cross-section area times length. Add non-overlapping solid parts; subtract removed parts.
cards.remember_en: V = (4 × 2/2) × 5. The answer is 20.

cards.question_en: Read timetables and convert fractional time.
cards.idea_en: Read timetables and convert fractional time.
steps_en: The trip leaves at 8:40 am and arrives at 9:25 am on the same day.
Count to 9:00, then to 9:25. Convert hours into 60-minute units.
20 + 25 = 45 minutes = 3/4 hour. Keep time units consistent.
cards.remember_en: 1 × 60 + 14. The answer is 74.

cards.question_en: Distinguish radius, diameter, and circumference.
cards.idea_en: Distinguish radius, diameter, and circumference.
steps_en: A radius reaches from the centre to the circle.
A diameter contains two radii: d = 2r.
Circumference names the distance all the way around the circle.
cards.remember_en: d = 2 × 3. The answer is 6.

cards.question_en: Explain angle sums and solve unknown angles.
cards.idea_en: Explain angle sums and solve unknown angles.
steps_en: A pentagon can be split into three triangles from one vertex.
An n-sided polygon splits into n − 2 triangles; its interior sum is 180(n − 2)°.
Walking once around a polygon makes one full turn. Exterior angles total 360°.
cards.remember_en: 180 − 35 − 43. The answer is 102.

cards.question_en: Translate, reflect, rotate, and scale on a coordinate plane.
cards.idea_en: Translate, reflect, rotate, and scale on a coordinate plane.
steps_en: A transformation changes all vertices by one rule. The origin is the centre for these examples.
Reflection in the y-axis changes each x sign. Corresponding points stay the same distance from the axis.
Next translate the reflected triangle right 2. Doing that translation before the reflection gives a different result.
cards.remember_en: New x = -2 + 3. The answer is 1.

connects_from.label_en: Year 7 · Move a shape on a grid

cards.question_en: Use scale, coordinates, compass points, and turns.
cards.idea_en: Use scale, coordinates, compass points, and turns.
steps_en: A map scale compares map distance with real distance. Check its units first.
Start at (1, 1). Move three squares east, then two squares north to (4, 3).
The route has five steps. At 2 km per step, the route is 10 km long.
cards.remember_en: 4 × 3. The answer is 12.

cards.question_en: Name variable types and collect useful data.
cards.idea_en: Name variable types and collect useful data.
steps_en: Categories label choices. Discrete values count. Continuous values measure.
Define who is measured, what is measured, the unit, and the method before collecting.
Describe the group you actually measured. Three measurements do not describe every child.
cards.remember_en: The variable is categorical. Use this data type when choosing a graph.

cards.question_en: Find mean, median, mode, and range.
cards.idea_en: Find mean, median, mode, and range.
steps_en: There are five values: 2, 2, 4, 6, 6. Repeats count as separate observations.
The mean shares the total equally. The median is the middle sorted value.
Range = 6 − 2 = 4. Both 2 and 6 are modes; a dataset can have several modes.
cards.remember_en: Total 22; divide by 4. The answer is 11/2.

cards.question_en: Match graphs to variables and show time order.
cards.idea_en: Match graphs to variables and show time order.
steps_en: A bar graph compares category frequencies; a categorical dot plot can show one dot per observation.
Clustered or stacked bars preserve both variables. The legend identifies each group.
Put time in order. Label the measured variable and unit so the trend has meaning.
cards.remember_en: Read the count against the vertical scale. The answer is 4.

cards.question_en: Explain an unusual point and its effect on summaries.
cards.idea_en: Explain an unusual point and its effect on summaries.
steps_en: Most values lie together; one unusually distant point may be an outlier.
A high outlier pulls the mean and stretches the range. The median is less affected, not always unchanged.
The long right tail gives positive skew. Check unusual observations before keeping or correcting them.
cards.remember_en: Most values are between 3 and 5. The answer is 35.

cards.question_en: Summarise graphs and notice missing or misleading information.
cards.idea_en: Summarise graphs and notice missing or misleading information.
steps_en: Read the title, population, axes, units, and scale before describing a pattern.
The four counts total 64, so the mean is 16 visitors per day. Range is 8.
These data describe four days. Missing dates, units, or scale can block a sound interpretation.
cards.remember_en: Total = 26 across four days. The answer is 13/2.

cards.question_en: Run trials, estimate chance, and compare with a model.
cards.idea_en: Run trials, estimate chance, and compare with a model.
steps_en: Experimental probability uses outcome count divided by total trials. Unknown biased objects need experiments.
For a fair coin, theoretical P(heads) = 1/2. Experimental proportions vary across sets of trials.
Large samples tend to approach the model probability, but improvement is not guaranteed after every added trial.
cards.remember_en: 15/40. The answer is 3/8.

cards.question_en: List outcomes and calculate an event and its complement.
cards.idea_en: List outcomes and calculate an event and its complement.
steps_en: For independent fair devices, start with H or T and then list each spinner result.
Six ordered pairs are equally likely. An event can contain one pair or several pairs.
H1 is one of six outcomes. P(H1) = 1/6; P(not H1) = 5/6. They add to one.
cards.remember_en: 3 favourable counters out of 8. The answer is 3/8.

frames.title: Equal jumps
frames.caption: Counting in fours means adding four with each jump.
frames.alt: A number line with equally spaced multiples of four.

frames.title: Go backwards too

frames.title: Start anywhere

frames.alt: 137, 147, 157 have the same ones digit.

try_it.prompt: When counting backwards in fours, what changes each time?
try_it.feedback_en: Equal backward jumps subtract four every time.
try_it.explain_en: Equal backward jumps subtract four every time.
try_it.alt: The sequence counts backwards in fours.

frames.title: Pairs or one left
frames.caption: Even numbers make pairs; odd numbers leave one unpaired.
frames.alt: Eight dots in four pairs, compared with nine dots including one extra.

frames.title: Add three

frames.alt: The multiples three, six, nine alternate odd, even, odd.

frames.title: Find shared stops
frames.caption: Twos and fives meet at multiples of ten.
frames.alt: Shared stops at ten and twenty on a counting line.

try_it.prompt: After an odd number, adding three gives what?
try_it.feedback_en: Odd plus three changes the pairing: the total becomes even.
try_it.explain_en: Odd plus three changes the pairing: the total becomes even.
try_it.alt: The multiples three, six, nine alternate odd, even, odd.

frames.title: Fill to one hundred
frames.caption: The missing part joins the known part to make 100.
frames.alt: Ten equal sections represent a hundred; three sections represent thirty.

frames.title: Bridge through a ten
frames.caption: From 34, add six to 40, then sixty more.
frames.alt: Jumps from 34 to 40, then to 100, total 66.

frames.title: Scale a known fact
frames.caption: Three plus four also helps us combine hundreds.
frames.alt: Seven hundred-blocks show three hundreds plus four hundreds.

try_it.prompt: What whole are we making in 34 + __ = 100?
try_it.feedback_en: The known part and missing part must fill the whole of one hundred.
try_it.explain_en: The known part and missing part must fill the whole of one hundred.
try_it.alt: Jumps from 34 to 40, then to 100, total 66.

frames.title: Line up the places
frames.caption: Place ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds.
frames.alt: 137 plus 54 arranged in aligned H, T, O columns.

frames.title: Exchange ten ones
frames.caption: Seven ones plus four ones make one ten and one one.
frames.alt: Eleven dots: ten grouped together and one separate.

frames.title: Combine the columns
frames.caption: The exchanged ten joins the tens; the total is 191.
frames.alt: The aligned sum is 191, including the exchanged ten.

try_it.prompt: Eleven ones can be exchanged for what?
try_it.feedback_en: Ten ones become one ten, with one one left over.
try_it.explain_en: Ten ones become one ten, with one one left over.
try_it.alt: Eleven dots: ten grouped together and one separate.

frames.title: Keep the columns aligned
frames.caption: Subtract matching place values, starting with the ones column.
frames.alt: 243 minus 56 aligned by place value.

frames.title: Rename without changing
frames.caption: Exchange one ten so thirteen ones can lose six ones.
frames.alt: 243 is renamed as two hundreds, three tens, thirteen ones.

frames.title: Exchange and check
frames.caption: Another exchange lets us subtract tens; check by adding back.
frames.alt: 243 minus 56 equals 187; addition checks the subtraction.

try_it.prompt: Can we rename one ten as ten ones without changing the amount?
try_it.feedback_en: Exchanging changes how the amount is grouped, but not its value.
try_it.explain_en: Exchanging changes how the amount is grouped, but not its value.
try_it.alt: 243 is renamed as two hundreds, three tens, thirteen ones.

frames.title: Track the starting amount
frames.caption: A bus starts with 28 children before anyone moves.
frames.alt: Four equal groups of seven represent 28 children.

frames.title: Apply each change
frames.caption: Twelve get on, then nine get off the bus.
frames.alt: Changes from 28 to 40 and from 40 to 31.

frames.title: Check the story
frames.caption: The final amount is 31 children, not both changes added.
frames.alt: The before-change-after table gives 31 children.

try_it.prompt: Children get on, then some get off. Which plan fits?
try_it.feedback_en: Getting on increases the number; getting off decreases it.
try_it.explain_en: Getting on increases the number; getting off decreases it.
try_it.alt: Changes from 28 to 40 and from 40 to 31.

frames.title: Equal rows
frames.caption: Each row has four counters, and there are three rows.
frames.alt: Three rows of four dots.

frames.title: Add equal groups
frames.caption: Repeated addition counts every row once, giving twelve counters.
frames.alt: Three equal rows are counted by adding four three times.

frames.title: Write multiplication
frames.caption: Three groups of four can be written as three times four.
frames.alt: The array connects three groups of four to 3 times 4 equals 12.

try_it.prompt: An array has three rows of four. What does three count?
try_it.feedback_en: Three counts the equal groups. Four counts the dots in each group.
try_it.explain_en: Three counts the equal groups. Four counts the dots in each group.
try_it.alt: Three rows of four dots.

frames.title: Begin with the whole
frames.caption: Twelve counters can be shared into three equal groups.
